The purpose of this notebook is to explore the results from the storm surge
exposure analysis. For each of 4 CMIP6 models we compute the change in 100-year
return period storm surge level (future 2021-2050 minus historical 1985-2014).
Each NPS water supply is assigned the worst-case model surge change from its
nearest coastal station, divided by distance to coast. Water supplies whose
nearest surge station is more than 50 km away receive NA.

Data are generated in `rapid_workflow.Rmd` using `calc_storm_surge_exposure()`.
Raw surge stations are preprocessed by `process_storm_surge_data()`.

# Interpretation

`raw_surge_change_max` is the change in the 100-year return period (RP100) surge
height (in meters) at the nearest coastal model node, computed as future
(2021–2050) minus historical (1985–2014) under SSP5-8.5, divided by
`shore_dist_m` (distance to coast in meters). The division weights exposure by
coastal proximity: the same surge change matters more for a supply close to the
coast than one near the 50 km boundary.

The worst-case value across the 4 CMIP6 models is retained for each station, so
`raw_surge_change_max` reflects the most adverse projected outcome rather than
a model mean.

The metric captures only the *change in surge dynamics* driven by altered storm
climatology; it does not include mean sea level rise, which is addressed
separately by the sea level rise inundation indicator.

Water supplies more than 50 km from the nearest coastal surge station receive
`NA` — they are considered outside the domain of meaningful coastal surge
exposure regardless of surge magnitude at the nearest station.

# Data source

Source: Muis et al. (2023), distributed through the Copernicus Climate Data
Store (CDS), dataset `storm_surge_muis_2023/` (local path).

## What was downloaded

| Field | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Model** | CMCC-CM2-VHR4, EC-Earth3P-HR, HadGEM3-GC31-HM, HadGEM3-GC31-HM-SST | High-resolution HighResMIP models — chosen because coarse models underestimate tropical cyclone-driven surges |
| **Period** | 1985–2014 (historical), 2021–2050 (future) | Historical baseline vs. near-future projection window |
| **Variable** | Surge level | Meteorological surge component in meters — not total water level, not SLR |
| **Statistic** | 100-year return period (RP100), best-fit bound | Upper-tail surge height representative of a 1-in-100-year event over each 30-year period |
| **Experiment** | Historical, Future | Historical = ERA5-forced run; Future = SSP5-8.5 forced run |
| **Derived variable** | Absolute value | Actual surge height in meters — not already a change value; the change is computed in `process_storm_surge_data()` |

## What we are trying to calculate: 

How much storm surge is projected to change at 
a given water supply. We are not considering tides and mean sea level rise as a 
part of this analysis. 

## How we are calculating this risk: 

The Global Tide and Surge Model v3.0 (GTSM) is 
a 2D hydrodynamic model. For each climate model run, hourly wind speed and surface
pressure fields are used to force GTSM, which sumulates the resulting surge height
at ~43,000 coastal stations globally (roughly one every ~5-10km along coastlines).

Over each 30-year period GTSM produces a time series of hourly surge heights at
each coastal station. The 100-year return period (RP100) is the surge height
expected to be exceeded on average once every 100 years — an extreme but
plausible event.

For each of the 4 models, `process_storm_surge_data()` computes:

```
surge_change = future_rp100 (2021–2050) − historical_rp100 (1985–2014)
```

The worst-case value across the 4 models is retained per station. 
`calc_storm_surge_exposure()` then assigns each water supply the surge change 
from its nearest station, with a 50 km distance cutoff.

# Establish environment

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
source("setup.R")
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
```

# Load data

## Water supplies

```{r}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)
```

## Storm surge stations (preprocessed CONUS subset)

```{r}
storm_surge_stations <- sf::st_read(
  here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "storm_surge", "storm_surge_exposure_conus.gpkg"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

## Storm surge exposure results

Check for a saved CSV first; fall back to running the calc function if none exists.

```{r}
exp_files <- list.files(
  here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
  pattern    = "^storm_surge_exposure_.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(exp_files) > 0) {
  storm_surge_exp <- read_csv(exp_files[length(exp_files)], show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  storm_surge_exp <- calc_storm_surge_exposure(
    water_supplies       = water_supplies,
    storm_surge_stations = here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "storm_surge",
                                "storm_surge_exposure_conus.gpkg"),
    save       = TRUE,
    output_dir = here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
    verbose    = TRUE
  )
}
```

## Join results to water supply geometries

```{r}
ws_mapped <- water_supplies %>%
  inner_join(
    storm_surge_exp %>% select(-park_unit, -park_name),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )
```

# Maps

## Water supplies and surge stations colored by worst-case surge change

Higher values (red) indicate greater projected storm surge increase. Grey points
are water supplies more than 50 km from the nearest surge station
(`raw_surge_change_max = NA`).

```{r}
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

ws_exposed <- ws_mapped %>% filter(!is.na(raw_surge_change_max))
ws_distant <- ws_mapped %>% filter(is.na(raw_surge_change_max))

mapview(ws_exposed,
        zcol        = "norm_surge_change_max",
        col.regions = pal,
        layer.name  = "Storm Surge Change (norm)",
        popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
          sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_exposed) %>%
            select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                   raw_surge_change_max,
                   norm_surge_change_max,
                   rank_surge_change_max)
        )) +
  mapview(ws_distant,
          col.regions = "grey60",
          color       = "grey60",
          layer.name  = ">50 km from surge station",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_distant) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                     raw_surge_change_max,
                     norm_surge_change_max,
                     rank_surge_change_max)
          )) 
```

## CONUS storm surge stations colored by worst-case surge change

```{r}
mapview(storm_surge_stations,
        zcol        = "max_surge_change_m",
        col.regions = pal,
        layer.name  = "Surge change (m)",
        popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
          sf::st_drop_geometry(storm_surge_stations) %>%
            select(lon, lat, max_surge_change_m, max_surge_model)
        ))
```
